newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cabinet replaces Bulgargas board.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cabinet replaces Bulgargas board.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday replaced the board of the country's state-owned gas monopoly Bulgargas.
The decision was motivated by the fact that the board of directors had to be restructured and its number reduced to seven from nine members.

The new members of the board are the energy ministry chief expert Anguel Semerdjiev, the industry ministry legal department chief Pavel Marinov and Gazenergo's executive director Alexander Belovezhdov, Bulgargas former deputy executive director, a government spokeswoman said.
The energy minister Roumen Ovcharov was dropped from the directors' board.

Bulgargas said on Thursday it was reducing supplies to almost half of its major industrial customers who had not paid their bills, including the country's giants the Neftohim oil refinery and the Kremikovtsi steelworks.

Under a deal approved by the previous cabinet in 1994, Bulgaria's holding Multigroup subsidiaries Kreditna Banka and Discontova Kashta were due to buy 2.53 billion levs worth of debts owed to Bulgargas by industrial giants Kremikovtsi Metal Works and Himko Chemical Plant at a discount of 25 percent.

The Socialist cabinet have ruled against the deal, demanding that all payments due be paid to Bulgargas. But the Constitutional court ruled last year in favour of Multigroup. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
